dataset.name: COMPASS-FME Terrestrial Ecosystem Manipulation to Probe the Effects of Storm Treatments (TEMPEST) Soil Greenhouse Gas Fluxes 04/2020-06/2024
description: Both raw and processed data measured using a LI-COR 7810 Greenhouse Gas Analyzer in the TEMPEST experiment, part of COMPASS-FME (https://compass.pnnl.gov/FME/COMPASSFME), at Smithsonian Environmental Research Center. This ecosystem-scale experiment probes the effects of saltwater versus freshwater flooding in a coastal deciduous forest.

The data consist of both concentrations and fluxes of carbon dioxide and methane measured using static chambers on the soil surface, approximately every two weeks from early 2020 to mid 2024. Some of the measurement points are controls, and some subject to root-exclusion techniques; all measurements are embedded in the TEMPEST control, freshwater, and saltwater plots (see Hopple et al. 2023). These data were generated to understand changing soil greenhouse gas (CO2 and CH4) production and consumption. File types are comma-separated value (.csv) for data, and markdown (.md) for supplementary information.

measurementTechnique: Soil CO2 and CH4 flux measurements were collected approximately twice per month for four years (April 2020–June 2024). A 20 cm-diameter PVC collar was permanently installed to a depth of ∼6 cm at the center of each subplot (see Hopple et al. 2023) and measurements were taken using an infrared gas analyzer (IRGA; LI-7810, LI-COR Inc., Lincoln, NE) with a 20 cm-diameter soil chamber attached (LI-8201 Smart Chamber). The chamber volume was 4,244.1 cm3 with no fan and fluxes based on an internal chamber thermocouple. The IRGA measured concentrations every second over a 1-min period and calculated the flux as the exponential regression of gas accumulation in the closed chamber system over unit area and time (μmol m−2 s−1 for CO2; nmol m−2 s−1 for CH4); two successive measurements were taken at each collar. Soil volumetric water content (VWC), temperature, and electrical conductivity (EC) were also recorded at 5 cm depth during each flux measurement using auxiliary sensors attached to the LI-7810 (6000-09TC probe). Fluxes were measured at various times of the day, but most often in the mid-morning, which typically is representative of average daily fluxes. The collar measurement order was randomized. All subplots were established in areas free of aboveground woody plants. Data were processed using the fluxfinder R package (Wilson et al. 2024).
